newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka to reintroduce insurance in former rebel area.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka to reintroduce insurance in former rebel area.

text.p: Sri Lanka will reintroduce insurance schemes in the former Tamil Tiger rebel stronghold of Jaffna after a seven-year break, the Weekend Express newspaper said on Saturday.

It said the Sri Lanka Insurance Corporation (SLIC) would soon launch schemes to cover riots, strikes, civil commotion and terrorism, helping to increase private sector participation in the reconstruction work in Jaffna.
Marine insurance in full would also be provided for shipment of consumer goods and material needed for reconstruction work, the paper added.
All goods are transported to Jaffna by either air or ship as there is still no direct road linking the northern peninsula with rest of the island.
The paper said renewed insurance would make it easy for civilians to obtain bank loans to rebuild their homes.

It said the SLIC terminated insurance coverage in the northern region after fighting erupted between the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) and government troops in that part of the country in 1990.
Insurance officials were not immediately available for comment.
The Sri Lankan military captured Jaffna town in December 1995. The rebels are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The military wrested control of the entire peninsula four months later, pushing the rebels further south into the brush jungle of the Wanni.
The government said earlier this week that nearly 500,000 civilians who fled the war have returned to Jaffna and reconstruction work in the once devastated area was in full swing.
The military launched a huge offensive against the rebels in May to open a strategic highway through the Wanni to link Jaffna with the rest of the island.
But the offensive has slowed down since the LTTE launched two fierce counterattacks in two weeks last month.
